newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi shares drop 2.12 percent in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi shares drop 2.12 percent in moderate trade.

text.p: Saudi shares dropped 2.12 percent in moderate trade in the week to Thursday, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Saturday.

The index ended at 160.87 points from 164.35 points a week earlier. The value of traded stocks edged down to 859.6 million riyals from 903 million the previous week. Some 3.94 million shares changed hands, down from 3.99 million.
Of the 59 companies traded, eight rose, 42 declined and nine were unchanged.
Services sector shares dominated trade, accounting for 38 percent of volume, followed by banks with 20 percent and cement stocks with 15 percent.
The week's top performer was the Saudi Advanced Industries Co (SAIC), which gained 9.7 percent to close at 68 riyals. Advertising and public relations company Tihama rose 5.1 percent to 62 riyals.
Savola, the country's biggest food group, chalked up 3.6 percent and closed at 491 riyals.
The week's leading decliner was glass company Zoujaj, which slid 10 percent to 153 riyals. The previous week Zoujaj had been among the market's top gainers, rising to 170 riyals from 155.

The Saudi Public Transportation Company (SAPTCO) dropped 9.9 percent to end the week at 100 riyals. Saudi Hotels lost 9.7 percent to close at 131 riyals after gaining 9.8 percent to 145 riyals the previous week.
The week's most active stock in terms of volume was Makkah Construction and Development Co, which accounted for 11.9 percent of trade volume. ($1=3.75 riyals)
